definition: Holos was an influential OLAP (Online Analytical Processing) product of the 1990s.
details: Developed by Holistic Systems in 1987, the product remained in use until around 2004. The core of the Holos Server was a business intelligence (BI) virtual machine. The Holos Language was a very broad language in that it covered a wide range of statements and concepts, including the reporting system, business rules, OLAP data, SQL data (using the Embedded SQL syntax within the hosting HL), device properties, analysis, forecasting, and data mining. Holos Server provided an array of different, but compatible, storage mechanisms for its multi-cube architecture: memory, disk, SQL. It was therefore the first product to provide "hybrid OLAP" (HOLAP). The Holos Client was both a design and delivery vehicle, and this made it quite large. Around about 2000, the Holos Language was made object-oriented (HL++) with a view to allowing the replacement of the Holos Client with a custom Java or VB product. However, the company were never sold on this, and so the project was abandoned. Before its demise, the Holos Server product ran under Windows NT (Intel and Alpha), VMS (VAX and Alpha), plus about 10 flavors of UNIX, and accessed over half-a-dozen different SQL databases. It was also ported to se

explainer.lead: Holos was an influential OLAP product of the 1990s, developed by Holistic Systems from 1987 and in use until around 2004. It matters as an early example of a broad business intelligence platform built around a BI virtual machine.

tiers.eli5: Think of a powerful spreadsheet server that not only stored data but also ran reports, rules, and forecasts from one place.
tiers.practitioner: Its Holos Language covered a wide range of statements and concepts, including the reporting system, business rules, OLAP data, SQL data via Embedded SQL, device properties, analysis, forecasting, and data mining. The Holos Server provided an array of different capabilities on top of a BI virtual machine.
tiers.paperLevel: It is a commercial OLAP product, not a formal algorithm; its specification is its language, which spans reporting, rules, data access, analysis, forecasting, and mining.

explainer.example: An analyst could define OLAP data, attach business rules, and run a forecast using statements in the Holos Language on a Holos Server.
